messages:
Anya K: Quick sync — thinking through warmup window for the preflight prober. We need to balance cache priming vs cost and avoid masking regressions. Thoughts?
Mike H: Agree. Warmup helps KV cache and kernel JIT warm paths, but it can hide cold-start regressions.
Chen L: For benching we saw 30-60s warmup reduces tail latency by ~18% on p99 for some models. But it doubled probe cost.
Lina R: From infra POV we care about three failure modes: cold-start regressions, degraded throughput after autoscale, and cache corruption. Warmup reduces first two but not third.
Samir P: Product concern: if warmup hides regressions, we might ship a bad model. Can we record warmed vs cold metrics separately?
Anya K: Yes — proposal: prober has two phases, warmup-phase (N warmup requests) and measurement-phase. Record both sets independently and fail on measurement-phase thresholds. Warmup only used to stabilize noise.
Mike H: Suggest warmup window configurable per-model-type. Small models: 5 requests; L > 8B: 30 requests. Use exponential backoff if warmup hits error rate.
Chen L: Sampling strategy: deterministic golden inputs + random fuzzed samples. Golden covers core behavior; fuzzing finds regressions that affect distribution. Both needed.
Samir P: Can we annotate golden inputs with expected tokens / tolerance? Some models will rephrase. Need fuzzy metrics not exact match.
Anya K: Right. Metrics: p95/p99 latency, token-efficiency (tokens/response), and semantic drift (embedding cosine vs baseline) with threshold 0.88 as fail condition for golden set.
Lina R: Operationally we should schedule prober runs to avoid peak autoscale windows. Maybe align with non-peak hours and use capacity-aware routing.
Mike H: Implementation sketch for scheduler config:
```
prober:
  cadence: hourly
  warmup_requests: 20
  measurement_requests: 50
  capacity_tolerance: 0.15  # fraction of pool reserved
  avoid_peak: true
```
Use a "capacity_tolerance" to reserve fractional capacity so probes don't evict real traffic.
Chen L: Also add a randomized jitter to cadence to avoid thundering herd across many models.
Anya K: Fallback policy: if measurement-phase fails, auto-fallback to previous pinned model for X minutes and create an incident ticket. But we should avoid flip-flopping for noisy signals.
Samir P: Rate-limit auto-fallbacks: at most 1 auto-fallback per model per 24h, require manual sign-off after 3 auto-fallbacks in a week.
Lina R: For cache consistency issue detection, include a small set of stateful probes that validate KV outputs across repeated calls and across shard boundaries. If detected, trigger infra alert (not auto-fallback).
Mike H: Edge case: quantized variants may have acceptable latency but degrade quality in ways embedding-metrics miss. Add lightweight human-review gate if semantic drift flag fires but latency ok.
Anya K: Good point. Separate severity levels: severity=blocker (rollback), warning (alert + monitoring), info (annotate).
Chen L: We should store full prober traces in S3 for 30 days with tag: model@version@run_ts for postmortem debugging.
Anya K: Cost tradeoffs: estimate probe cost per model per day = (warmup+measurement) * avg_token_cost * runs_per_day. We'll surface a cost budget per customer/model to avoid surprises.
Samir P: UX: expose a "sensitivity" slider per model: conservative (small warmup, stricter thresholds), aggressive (larger warmup, looser thresholds). Defaults tuned by model size and dataset.
Lina R: Ops checklist before enabling prober on Private deploys: KMS key access, network egress controls for golden check (if external embedding service used), and runbook for rollback.
Anya K: Action items: 1) Mike - prototype scheduler + capacity_tolerance (this week). 2) Chen - finalize golden/fuzz sample set and metric thresholds. 3) Lina - add infra alert hooks and runbook. 4) Samir - draft UX copy for sensitivity slider.
Mike H: I'll open a PR with the scheduler skeleton and a small local test harness.
Chen L: I'll share candidate golden inputs in the bench repo and synthetic fuzz rules.
Lina R: I'll draft runbook and playbook steps for rollback and incident communication.
infra-bot: NOTE: A prober job was scheduled for model: "mosaic-8b-v2" at 2024-06-15T09:22:00Z (dry-run).
Anya K: Excellent. Let's reconvene after PR + sample set. Thanks everyone :thanks:
